strategy.summary: At buggy commit 16f5942, pcl::ProgressiveMorphologicalFilter stores/returns max_window_size as int (getMaxWindowSize/setMaxWindowSize), so a fractional coordinate-space maximum such as 6.25f is truncated to 6. The PR adds a new gtest (ProgressiveMorphologicalFilter.FractionalMaximumWindowSize) that static_asserts the getter returns float and EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(getMaxWindowSize(), 6.25f). Reproduce by adding only that test file plus its CMakeLists registration on top of the buggy headers, building the segmentation tests, and running the test: it must fail (compile-time static_assert failure at the buggy revision), and pass once max_window_size_ is float.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: 6 (int magnitude; the fractional part 0.25 is truncated because getMaxWindowSize/setMaxWindowSize use int)
Compile-time static assertion failure: decltype(filter.getMaxWindowSize()) is int, not float

input_output_examples.input: ProgressiveMorphologicalFilter: compare window_size = cell_size * (2 * base^iteration + 1) against a fractional coordinate-space maximum, e.g. 6.25 m
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Maximum stored as int (e.g. 6), truncating the fractional threshold and cutting off valid fractional maximum window dimensions
input_output_examples.expected_output: Maximum kept as float 6.25 in the same coordinate-space units as window_size, honoring the fractional threshold

environment_setup: Ubuntu 24.04-style Linux host (CI base image pointcloudlibrary/env:24.04); any CMake >= 3.10 and a C++17 compiler (clang-18 at /usr/bin/clang-18 per CI, GCC acceptable).
Install PCL build dependencies: Eigen3, Boost (system), FLANN, VTK/OpenNI optional; the test target only links pcl_gtest and pcl_segmentation, so minimal deps suffice.
Fetch available LLVM toolchain if clang-18 is absent, matching CI: bash -c "$(wget -O - https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh)".
pcl_gtest (bundled gtest) is provided by the repo; no external gtest package is required.
build_steps: Apply ONLY the test-side changes from PR #6461: create test/segmentation/test_progressive_morphological_filter.cpp (33 lines, gtest ProgressiveMorphologicalFilter.FractionalMaximumWindowSize) and add the PCL_ADD_TEST(progressive_morphological_filter test_progressive_morphological_filter FILES ... LINK_WITH pcl_gtest pcl_segmentation) block to test/segmentation/CMakeLists.txt. Do NOT touch either progressive_morphological_filter.h header.

mkdir build && cd build; cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_global_tests=ON -DBUILD_segmentation=ON -DBUILD_tools=OFF -DBUILD_examples=OFF (add -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang-18 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang-18 for CI parity).
Build the new test executable: cmake --build . --target test_progressive_morphological_filter -j$(nproc) (or make test_progressive_morphological_filter).
reproduction_steps: Confirm the buggy header declares the maximum as int: grep -n 'max_window_size_' segmentation/include/pcl/segmentation/progressive_morphological_filter.h should show 'int max_window_size_{33};' and getMaxWindowSize()/setMaxWindowSize(int) signatures.
Add the PR test file and CMakeLists registration as described (test-only patch), leaving headers at the buggy revision.

Configure and build as above; observe that compilation of test_progressive_morphological_filter.cpp fails on the static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(filter.getMaxWindowSize()), float>) because the getter returns int at the buggy revision. Capture the compiler error as the failing observation.

To also observe the runtime numeric truncation, temporarily comment out only the static_assert in the local copy of the test (do not change the library), rebuild, and run the binary: setMaxWindowSize(6.25f) is converted to int 6, so EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(filter.getMaxWindowSize(), 6.25f) reports 6 vs 6.25 and the test FAILS.
Verify no other test in the segmentation suite is affected, then record the failure output as the reproduction evidence.
strategy.expected_buggy_behavior: At 16f5942 the test does not compile: static_assert(is_same_v<decltype(filter.getMaxWindowSize()), float>) fails because max_window_size_/getMaxWindowSize are int; if the static_assert is bypassed, setMaxWindowSize(6.25f) truncates to 6 and EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(getMaxWindowSize(), 6.25f) fails with 6 vs 6.25. The ctest target progressive_morphological_filter thus reports failure.
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: With max_window_size_ changed to float (b2873a1) and getMaxWindowSize()/setMaxWindowSize(float), the static_assert holds and setMaxWindowSize(6.25f) preserves 6.25f, so EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(filter.getMaxWindowSize(), 6.25f) passes and ctest -R progressive_morphological_filter reports all tests passed.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy commit (with only the PR test file + CMakeLists registration applied), building/running ProgressiveMorphologicalFilter.FractionalMaximumWindowSize fails: compile error on the float static_assert, or (static_assert bypassed) EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ 6 vs 6.25 failure; the same test passes once the header is fixed.
risks_or_ambiguities: The reproducing test file test/segmentation/test_progressive_morphological_filter.cpp is NEW in PR #6461 and therefore absent at the buggy commit; the test-only part of the diff must be applied manually before reproduction.

Because the test uses static_assert on the return type, the buggy failure is a COMPILE failure of the test target, not a runtime EXPECT failure; the runtime 6-vs-6.25 truncation is only observable if the static_assert is locally removed.

Exact buggy signatures of getMaxWindowSize/setMaxWindowSize (int vs float parameter) are inferred from the PR diff text ('int max_window_size_{33}' -> 'float max_window_size_{33.0f}'); verify in the header before running.

CMake option names for enabling tests (BUILD_global_tests) and the resulting ctest name for PCL_ADD_TEST(progressive_morphological_filter ...) are inferred; confirm with 'ctest -N | grep progressive_morphological_filter'.
CI evidence is the clang-tidy GitHub Actions workflow (Q4 confidence 0.4), not a build/test workflow; compiler/build flags are best-effort and other compilers should produce the same failure.
The ApproximateProgressiveMorphologicalFilter header is also modified by the PR but is intentionally kept int (grid-cell counts) and has no covering test here.
